newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi index closes 2.24 pct up on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Delhi index closes 2.24 pct up on foreign buying.

text.p: The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed up 20.35 points, or 2.24 percent, at 935.17 points on Wednesday on strong buying by foreign institutional investors, brokers said.
Traders said foreign institutional investors concentrated on a select band of blue-chip stocks.
"Foreign buying was mainly restricted to multinational companies throughout the session," said one broker.
Shree Bhagwan Garg of brokers Means Leasing said: "The shortage of floating stocks in blue chips due to book closures also fuelled speculative buying."
Brokers said strong institutional buying also tempted small investors to make purchases, which further lifted share prices.
Reliance Industries closed 2.75 rupees higher at 366. The share had leapt to 367.90 in early trade before profit taking trimmed gains, brokers said.
Nestle India ended 15.50 rupees higher at 335.
Larsen and Toubro edged up 4.00 rupees to 261.
